title: Later Zhao
capsule: Later Zhao was a Jie-ruled state in northern China during the Sixteen Kingdoms period, founded by Shi Le (r. 319–333), a former slave of Jie ethnicity who rose through military service in Han-Zhao before breaking away and defeating his former masters in 329. At its height Later Zhao held most of the North China Plain, Inner Mongolia, and Shandong, vassalizing Former Liang and Dai while locked in stalemate with Eastern Jin south of the Huai River. Shi Le's nephew Shi Hu moved the capital to Yecheng in 335 and constructed elaborate palaces, but his court was notorious for violent purges. After Shi Hu's death in 349 a dynastic bloodbath wiped out most of the Shi family; the mixed-Han general Ran Min massacred the Jie population of Yecheng in 350, and Later Zhao collapsed by 351.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Later Zhao's territory is broadly documented in the Zizhi Tongjian and other Chinese dynastic sources, but precise border delineation with Eastern Jin and western rivals is approximate.
